NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — The intervention is a duty-cycle modulation of the catalyst circulation-rate setpoint to create periodic low-velocity rest periods that allow refractory self-healing. Standard practice maintains a constant circulation rate; this intervention introduces a controlled deceleration cycle that reduces cumulative erosion by enabling refractory surface recovery. The closest existing practice is continuous circulation optimization; this departs by introducing a scheduled low-velocity recovery period. The mechanism attacks the failure's driving physics by reducing the kinetic energy flux at the refractory-catalyst interface during each cycle, allowing micro-repair of eroded areas.

PHYSICS CHECK — The erosion rate E is proportional to catalyst kinetic energy flux: E ∝ ρ * v^3, where ρ is catalyst density and v is velocity. Reducing velocity by 50% during rest periods reduces erosion by 87.5% (0.5^3) in those intervals. Over a 4-hour cycle with 30 minutes at 50% velocity, cumulative erosion decreases by ~13% per cycle. DIRECTION-OF-EFFECT: driving variable = catalyst velocity; the mechanism moves it DOWN by 50% for 30 min every 4 h; this REDUCES the failure driver.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL — 
- (c) Modify existing circulation-rate control algorithm to implement 4-hour duty cycle: 3.5 h at nominal rate, 0.5 h at 50% rate (uses existing controller)
- (c) Set timer using existing control system timer function for 4-h cycle (no new hardware)
- (c) Program existing control system to execute circulation-rate ramp-down and ramp-up (±0.1%/s) during transitions

- Installation: Zero (uses existing control system and timer functions) — same as standard practice
- Commissioning: 4 hours (set timer and program logic) — same as standard practice retuning
- Operation: No additional labor — same as standard practice
- Maintenance: No additional maintenance — same as standard practice
- Operational loss: Zero (duty cycle occurs during normal operation, no production curtailment) — same as standard practice
Conclusion: Same burden class as standard practice (parameter retuning only).

EXECUTABLE TEST — Protocol: Run 30-day comparative test: (1) Baseline (constant circulation rate), (2) Intervention (4-h duty cycle). Instruments: Existing catalyst flow meters, pressure transmitters, and cyclone wall thermocouples. Pass/fail: Intervention shows ≥10% reduction in catalyst carryover fines (measured at primary cyclone outlet) and no increase in differential pressure across cyclone. Kill criterion: Any pressure fluctuation >5% nominal during ramp transitions. Duration: 30 days per phase.
